clusters.name: Failed or stalled runs fail silently: nobody gets told

quotes.author: Maya Lin (Orbit Health)
quotes.quote: Our scheduled agent errored at 2am. We only found out when the team asked where the report was.

quotes.author: Jonas Weber (Freightly)
quotes.quote: I need to know when the cron run breaks. Right now I check the console by hand every morning.

clusters.fix: API change: webhook events for session failed/errored/terminated on deployments, plus a default idle timeout on multiagent sub-threads that raises thread.idle_timeout to the coordinator and fires the same webhook; doc recipe "Get pinged when a scheduled run fails".

clusters.name: Can't reconstruct what a run did, which agent did it, or what it cost

quotes.author: karan
quotes.quote: I lost time digging through the trace to find out what happened

quotes.author: karan
quotes.quote: it cost money on a wasted thread.

quotes.author: karan
quotes.quote: a check that proves each agent did its job and what it cost

clusters.fix: API change: tag every session event with thread_id and agent name, carry a running token/cost total per thread in the event stream, and add a per-thread summary call (last step, wait state, cost) so which agent did what, and at what cost, is one API call, not a trace dig.

clusters.name: Recurring runs repeat stale work: no per-run 'today' and no memory of earlier runs

quotes.author: Lena Hoffmann (Parcelwise)
quotes.quote: It doesn't remember which carriers we already escalated

quotes.author: Lena Hoffmann (Parcelwise)
quotes.quote: so it re-flags them every day

clusters.fix: API change + doc: deployments inject run context (scheduled_for, run_number, last_successful_run_at) into each session; "Designing a recurring agent" guide separating per-run inputs from persistent memory-store state (items already handled).

clusters.name: No way to score agent quality over time or across changes

quotes.author: Dev Patel (Quillstack)
quotes.quote: We changed the instructions last week and I have a feeling the output got worse, but I can't prove it.

quotes.author: Omar Haddad (Stackly)
quotes.quote: I have no scoreboard. I tweak something, eyeball two outputs, and hope.

clusters.fix: API change: persist outcome grader verdicts/scores per session (and per multiagent thread), keyed by agent version, with a list/aggregate endpoint (score by version over time).

clusters.name: No obvious place for API keys, so they end up in the prompt

quotes.author: Sam Ortiz (Tallybook)
quotes.quote: I don't want the key in the prompt.

quotes.author: Sam Ortiz (Tallybook)
quotes.quote: What's the right place to put it so the agent can use it but can't leak it?

clusters.fix: Doc: "Where do API keys go?" vault quickstart (store in vault, reference from MCP connector/tool config), linked from agent creation, with an API warning when a key-shaped string appears in a system prompt or task.

clusters.name: Runaway run: no spend cap or stopping point
clusters.fix: API change: per-session budget cap on by default for scheduled deployments, webhook at 80% and at cap; pair with an outcome stop criterion.

clusters.name: Agent can't reach data inside the company's private network (VPC)
clusters.fix: Doc + reference skill: "Reach a database inside your VPC" with a self-hosted, outbound-only MCP server exposing a narrow read-only tool; creds in vault.

clusters.name: Coordinator hands work (or a placeholder) to the wrong sub-agent

quotes.author: karan
quotes.quote: sometimes calling the wrong agent for the task

quotes.author: karan
quotes.quote: It sent a placeholder to the wrong agent thread

clusters.fix: API change: handoff validation on multiagent sends. Each callable agent declares a role description and an input contract; a coordinator send whose payload is empty, a known placeholder, or fails the target's contract is rejected back to the coordinator with the list of agents and roles, instead of starting a wasted thread.

clusters.name: Can't tell whether each agent actually finished its job

quotes.author: karan
quotes.quote: I stopped trusting the result because I couldn't tell if the task was really done

quotes.author: karan
quotes.quote: a check that proves each agent did its job

clusters.fix: API change: outcome verdicts per multiagent thread: each sub-agent can carry its own outcome criteria, and the session returns a per-thread verdict record (criteria met yes/no, grader rationale, cost) the founder can read without opening the trace. Same persisted record as the no-quality-scoreboard fix.

clusters.name: Agent loses track of the task mid-run (context rot, botched memory)

quotes.author: karan
quotes.quote: the agent loses track of what it needs to be done

quotes.author: karan
quotes.quote: often context rot and memory gets botched

clusters.fix: Skill + guide: a "task ledger" skill that writes the plan and checklist to a memory store at the start of a run and re-reads/updates it before each step and after any context compaction, so the goal survives long sessions; guide "Keeping long-running agents on task".

clusters.name: Can't get output files out of a finished session

quotes.author: Maya Lin (Orbit Health)
quotes.quote: The agent says it wrote report.pdf to outputs, but I can't work out how to download it after the session.

quotes.author: Maya Lin (Orbit Health)
quotes.quote: The docs mention a scope thing I don't get.

clusters.fix: Doc: end-to-end "Get files out of a session" example (write to outputs, list session files, download after end) with plain-language file scope.

clusters.name: Sandbox dependency setup eats the first day

quotes.author: Lena Hoffmann (Parcelwise)
quotes.quote: Half my first day was fighting pip.

quotes.author: Lena Hoffmann (Parcelwise)
quotes.quote: The sandbox didn't have pandas and the install kept timing out.

clusters.fix: API change: environments declare packages installed once at build and cached across sessions, longer install timeout; preinstall pandas/numpy.

clusters.fix: Doc + skill: "Draft, then approve" pattern (no outbound-send tool or confirm-required policy, draft via files API, outcome = draft ready for review).
